competitors.name: mean_reversion
competitors.rules: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.

competitors.name: You
competitors.rules: Your real Robinhood account, rebased to the shared origin so it's comparable. Performance only — holdings and trades are deliberately not published.

competitors.name: congress_mirror
competitors.rules: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

regime.label: Restrictive rates with mixed risk appetite
regime.note: The federal-funds target remains 3.75%-4.00%. November 18 FOMC minutes and the December 8-9 meeting are the next dated policy catalysts. Low confidence and 70% cash reflect policy risk, binary event exposure, and the analyst book's weak long-run record.

analyst.thesis: Hold the two-name event book through its named catalysts instead of chasing the latest screen leaders. The analyst book is marked at $84.72, with -15.3 points of all-time alpha and a -2.77 annualized Sharpe. VRTX closed November 10 at $547.89 and remains positioned for the November 30 povetacicept PDUFA decision, 20 calendar days after the settled bar. The differentiated view is that a favorable label plus launch readiness can establish nephrology as a fifth commercial pillar faster than an approval-only framing credits. MSFT closed November 10 at $533.16 and Microsoft Ignite's agenda begins November 16, with the main event November 17-20. The differentiated view is that concrete agent-platform and monetization detail can reinforce the 48% Azure growth reported for FY27 Q1. MRNA, LLY, GILD, HD, REGN, and ABNB led the unlevered screen, but several are extended and MRNA remains up 289.13% over 60 sessions. Hold 18% VRTX, 12% MSFT, and 70% cash. This is the project's paper-portfolio bridge, not an official plugin investment recommendation.

evidence.point: The Federal Reserve's target range is 3.75%-4.00%, effective October 29, 2026; the October 27-28 meeting minutes are scheduled for November 18 and the next FOMC meeting is December 8-9.
Vertex reported Q3 2026 revenue of $3.44 billion, up 12%, and raised full-year revenue guidance to $13.15-$13.25 billion.
Vertex said povetacicept is under priority review with a November 30, 2026 PDUFA target date and would become its first commercial nephrology therapy if approved.
Vertex's Phase 3 materials reported a 49.8% povetacicept treatment effect at Week 36, with a 95% confidence interval of 39.2%-58.6% and P<0.0001.
Microsoft reported FY27 Q1 revenue of $92.3 billion, up 19%; Microsoft Cloud revenue was $63.9 billion, up 30%, and Azure revenue increased 48%.
Microsoft Ignite's official agenda begins November 16 and the main event runs November 17-20, 2026.
Robinhood reported trailing P/E ratios of 35.243603x for VRTX, 20.223280x for REGN, 47.054901x for LLY, 27.843870x for MSFT, 15.003028x for GOOGL, and 21.894323x for AMZN on November 11.
Through November 10, VRTX closed at $547.89 and MSFT at $533.16; over five sessions VRTX returned +3.23%, MSFT +2.34%, and SPY +0.20%.
Over 20 settled sessions through November 10, MRNA rose 15.99%, LLY 22.78%, GILD 15.52%, HD 19.42%, REGN 21.64%, and ABNB 12.88%; MRNA rose 289.13% over 60 sessions.

risks: Povetacicept approval is substantially anticipated after positive Phase 3 data; approval alone may not rerate VRTX.
A delay, rejection, restrictive label, or adverse safety interpretation at the November 30 PDUFA date invalidates the VRTX event thesis.
VRTX's Q3 spending increased as it invested in the renal franchise, Crinetics, and the JOURNAVX launch.
Microsoft Ignite may add no financially material information, while AI infrastructure spending can pressure margins.
The analyst book trails SPY by 15.3 points all-time and has a -2.77 Sharpe; the process has not earned higher deployment.
A 70% cash balance creates opportunity cost if risk assets rebound sharply.

rationale.VRTX: [DATA] VRTX closed November 10 at $547.89, 4.9% above the analyst book's $522.38 entry. Vertex reported Q3 revenue of $3.44 billion, up 12%, raised full-year guidance to $13.15-$13.25 billion, and has a November 30 povetacicept PDUFA date. Robinhood reported a 35.243603x trailing P/E versus 20.223280x for REGN. [ASSUMED] A favorable label plus launch readiness can establish a fifth commercial pillar faster than the market credits, but approval is partly anticipated and binary risk is high, so hold at 18%.
rationale.MSFT: [DATA] MSFT closed November 10 at $533.16, 0.5% above the analyst book's $530.41 entry. Microsoft reported FY27 Q1 revenue of $92.3 billion, Microsoft Cloud revenue of $63.9 billion, and 48% Azure growth. Robinhood reported a 27.843870x trailing P/E. Microsoft Ignite begins November 16, with the main event November 17-20. [ASSUMED] Concrete agent-platform and monetization detail can reinforce growth expectations, but the event may add no financially material disclosure and AI infrastructure spending remains a margin risk, so hold at 12%.

reflection.looking_back: The carried book entered the settled November 10 session with 18% VRTX, 12% MSFT, and 70% cash. The marked book moved from $85.03 to $84.72, about -0.36%, while SPY fell 0.37%, leaving roughly flat one-session alpha. The book still trails SPY by 15.3 points all-time and has a -2.77 annualized Sharpe.
worked: The 70% cash buffer limited the impact of MSFT's 2.20% decline and VRTX's 0.54% decline on November 10.
VRTX remains 4.9% above its $522.38 entry while its November 30 PDUFA catalyst remains ahead.
missed: The book still trails SPY by 15.3 points all-time with a -2.77 Sharpe; the process has not earned higher deployment.
MSFT gave back 2.20% on November 10, reducing its gain versus the $530.41 entry to 0.5% before Ignite.
reflection.adjustment: Keep both positions at existing weights through their named catalysts, retain 70% cash, and require event outcomes before increasing deployment.

swarm.note: Live swarm — 150 fish, each a unique trader profile shown its own random ~20-name slice of the watchlist (with recent headlines), voted via OpenRouter. Independent-voter election; dissenters (ringed) chose CASH.

live.note: Real money — the Agentic cash account (••••), funded ~$100 on 2026-06-29, running the funded algorithms (100% momentum_breakout) via run-robin with a per-order confirm gate. Figures here are the real, unscaled account.

rules.momentum_breakout: Buy a 20-day-high breakout confirmed by above-average volume; exit when price closes below its 20-day SMA. Few big winners, many small losers.
rules.mean_reversion: Buy when RSI(14) < 30 (oversold); sell when RSI(14) > 70 (overbought). Trades less, wins more often, smaller edge.
rules.blended_momo_rsi: Momentum breakout, but skip entries already overbought (RSI ≥ 70); exit on trend break or RSI > 75. Avoids chasing extended moves.
rules.deep_research_analyst: Holds the analyst's target weights; rebalanced each tick from a fresh research report (web + Robinhood data).
rules.llm_voters: Allocates across the swarm's top vote-getters (weight ∝ vote share, capped at 60%); rebalanced each tick.
rules.mirofish_real: Real-MiroFish: persona agents with memory interact over rounds, each ranking its best ideas; the panel's rank-weighted consensus (top 5 names, weight ∝ Borda points) rebalanced each tick.
rules.congress_mirror: Mirrors members of Congress from the kadoa STOCK Act disclosure mirror: follows every filer with a real track record and buys the in-universe names they disclosed purchasing within 120 days, weighting each name by how many distinct members bought it (consensus = conviction). Traded on the disclosure date — weeks after their actual fill.

sources.name: Standings, curves, decision trail (LIVE)
sources.detail: The forward paper test — every competitor trades a $100 book the same way, advanced one trading day per tick (rule strategies via tick.py / bot/engine.py; agents via run_agents.py / bot/paper.py), 5 bps slippage, −15% stop. Young — it grows one session per tick.

sources.name: Backtest reference
sources.detail: A separate Dec–Jun walk-forward backtest (2026-01-02–2026-11-10, in-sample, mostly-bull) is shown inside each rule strategy's detail for context only — it is NOT the live board.

sources.name: Research analyst
sources.detail: Agent-driven on the Claude Code plan: web_search + Robinhood data → one report (state/analyst.json) with target weights per tick. Sources link from each evidence row.

sources.name: Swarm vote
sources.detail: Independent-voter election: 150 unique-profile cheap models (DeepSeek/Gemini/Llama/Haiku via OpenRouter) each read one shared briefing and return a single ballot; tallied in bot/swarm.py. No interaction between fish.

sources.name: Real-MiroFish swarm
sources.detail: Social-simulation swarm (bot/mirofish.py): persona agents with memory interact over multiple rounds — each re-ranks its best ideas seeing its own prior view and its neighbours' latest — so a consensus forms via peer influence (the opposite of the independent swarm). The panel's rank-weighted (Borda) consensus becomes a multi-name book (top 5 names, weight ∝ points). Tiered cost (cheap/default/qwen); seeded from the briefing + optional world-events news.

sources.name: Live account
sources.detail: Robinhood MCP, Agentic cash account ••••, via get_portfolio / get_equity_positions / get_equity_orders.

sources.name: Display scale
sources.detail: The real paper books are $100 each; every dollar and share figure on this site is shown ×100 (a $10,000 book) so holdings read in whole shares and dollars. Per-share prices and percentages are unscaled.

sources.name: Luck baseline
sources.detail: 200 seeded random 5-name equal-weight buy-and-hold portfolios from the same universe, same sessions — the shaded band on the chart is their 10th–90th percentile. A strategy that never leaves the band hasn't shown anything luck can't.

sources.name: Graduation bar
sources.detail: The standing rule before any strategy earns real money at scale: ≥60 forward sessions, ≥20 decisions, max drawdown better than −20%, and positive excess return vs S&P 500. Tracked live on this board.
